text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- A World Bank delegation led by its Vice President starts a three-day working visit to Hanoi to introduce the rearrangement of World Bank's management structure and to conclude the credit-agreement for Phase 2 of Vietnam's highway upgrading project.

-- Yesterday the 47 million Singaporean dollar Saigon Floating Hotel sailed away from Ho Chi Minh city to a Philippines tourist island with a stop at Singapore port for repair. -- Between now and the year 2000, Vietnam hopes to decrease the number of children being sexually-abused by 50%-70% and reduce the number of children using drugs by 30%, according to the national children protection programme.
-- Vietnam's trade deficit in the first quarter of this year has narrowed to $849 million, according to statistics released by Ministry of Trade yesterday.
-- Today Vietnam's National Assembly spring section begins in Hanoi.
-- Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh told Canada's House of Commons delegation on April 1 that she was pleased with the rapid and diversified development of Vietnam-Canada bilateral relations.

-- On April 1 the Government issued a decision to allow the use of electronic documents such as recorded electronic tapes, disks and payment cards as evidence in settlements at banks and credit institutions.

-- On April 1 Ministry of Finance opened a Training Conference in Ho Chi Minh City focusing on the Law on State Budget with the participation of nearly 400 senior officials from southern provincial financial, tax and treasure departments.
